tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate move legality
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before adding a move, check that the chosen disk is the topmost disk on its source peg and that the destination peg is empty or has a larger top disk. This prevents size‑ordering violations and moving non‑top disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you generate a move, verify it respects the Tower of Hanoi rules.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a disk that is not the topmost on its source peg, or moving a disk onto a smaller disk.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use smallest disk as temporary buffer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Leverage disk 1 as a temporary holder because it can be placed on any peg without violating size constraints. Moving it aside frees pegs for larger disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you need a free peg to move other disks, move disk 1 to that peg first.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Leaving disk 1 on a peg that blocks the movement of larger disks, instead of moving it to a free peg.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Treat existing larger disks on target as base
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the goal peg already contains some of the largest disks in the correct order, keep them untouched and build the remaining tower on top. This avoids unnecessary moves that would disturb already‑correct parts of the final stack.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the target peg already has a partial correct stack of larger disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving a larger disk onto a peg that already has correctly placed larger disks, breaking the existing order.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final parseable list
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Make sure the last syntactically correct list in the response is the complete sequence of moves. Any earlier list will be ignored by the parser.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When writing the answer, place the move list at the very end and do not include any other list after it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Including an explanatory list after the move list, causing the parser to capture the wrong list.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Verify final configuration matches goal before outputting
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Mentally simulate all moves from the initial state and confirm that the final peg arrangement exactly matches the goal configuration. This catches errors that would otherwise go unnoticed until verification.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After constructing the move list, before submitting the answer.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Submitting a move list that leaves a disk on the wrong peg, so the final configuration does not match the goal.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive sub‑tower transfer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move a stack of k disks, recursively move the top k‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, move the largest disk, then move the k‑1 stack onto it. This systematic approach works for any sub‑tower.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to relocate a contiguous block of disks from one peg to another.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move a stack of three disks directly without first moving the top two, leading to illegal placements.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Avoid blocking future moves with temporary placements
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When using a disk as a temporary buffer, place it on a peg that will not need to be cleared for later essential moves. This prevents dead‑ends where a needed peg is occupied by a small disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During planning of intermediate moves, especially when the buffer peg might later need to be empty.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing disk 1 on a peg that later must be empty to receive a larger disk, causing a deadlock.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear target peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk onto it
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a larger disk onto a peg, ensure the peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk. This respects the rule that larger disks may never sit on smaller ones.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you intend to place a larger disk onto a peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 4 onto a peg where disk 2 is on top, violating size ordering.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Ensure final move list is the last list in the response
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Place the move list as the very last list in the output and avoid any trailing lists or text that could be parsed as a list. The parser selects the last syntactically correct list.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Appending a concluding remark that contains brackets, causing the parser to treat it as the final list.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear source peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a larger disk, first move any smaller disks that sit on top of it to another peg so that the larger disk becomes the topmost disk on its source peg. This guarantees the move is legal and prevents attempts to move a non‑top disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to move a disk that is not currently the top disk on its peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 5 while disk 4 remains on top of it, resulting in an illegal move.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model stops generation before emitting any moves, often due to premature termination or mis‑interpreting the answer format.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Explicitly write the move list, even if empty, and place it as the final list in the response.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk (size ordering violation)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model focuses on moving the right disk but forgets the size constraint, especially when trying to place a disk onto a peg that already contains a smaller top disk.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always check that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk before adding the move.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model selects a disk to move based on the goal without ensuring it is currently exposed on its peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: First clear any smaller disks that sit on top of the intended disk, using them as temporary buffers.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: Generation may be cut off by length limits or the model may think it has finished early.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: After drafting the moves, review the list to ensure it ends with the final move that achieves the goal.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a disk from a peg where it is not present
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model loses track of disk locations during multi‑step reasoning.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Maintain a mental (or written) representation of each peg’s contents after every move.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Including extra list after the final move list, causing the parser to select the wrong list
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model adds explanatory text or another list after the moves, which the parser interprets as the answer.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Terminate the response with the move list and avoid any additional bracketed structures afterwards.
